purpose: Place the four-jet selector theorem correctly between elementary subset-sum pigeonhole, zero-sum theory, coding syndromes, and Padé auxiliary-function construction.

classification.terminology_boundary: Subset-sum collision and finite abelian signature group are literal. Kernel is accurate only after extending the signatures to a homomorphism from Z^n; the binary selector map itself is not generally an F_2-linear code map.
nearest_prior_work: Olson's 1969 finite-abelian-group papers are foundational zero-sum antecedents, but their target is a nonempty zero-sum subsequence rather than equality of two binary subset sums with a signed difference.
Hamming's syndrome viewpoint gives the coding-theoretic analogy: more words than syndromes force a collision, but the mixed-exponent target here is not automatically a binary linear code.

Bombieri--Vaaler (1983) supplies a much stronger lattice/Siegel-lemma framework for bounded integer relations used in auxiliary-function mathematics; it does not give this exact binary cardinality threshold.
classification.attribution: Call the collision theorem elementary pigeonhole. Use zero-sum, syndrome, and Siegel-lemma sources only to orient neighboring traditions. Attribute the exact four-jet encoding, mixed-prime entropy budget, Lean API, and depth-41 130T+2S certificate to the local source.
classification.mathematical_interest: Low standalone depth but useful construction value: it quantifies exactly how many binary degrees of freedom buy four simultaneous local cancellations with coefficients bounded by one. Its proper digestion unit is a short method-boundary segment inside a broader auxiliary-function discussion.
classification.reusable_scope: Auxiliary-function constructions with finitely many additive local signatures, where bounded binary coefficients are preferable to solving an unrestricted integer linear system.
classification.why_it_matters: It separates the combinatorial cost of local cancellation from the analytic tasks of nonvanishing, height, and remainder control, preventing a selector collision from being mistaken for a completed Padé construction. That anti-overclaim boundary is more significant than the elementary collision itself.

mechanism_comparison.Pade_boundary: The theorem buys congruence cancellation only. It supplies none of the nonzero polynomial, analytic remainder, or height bounds required by an irrationality construction.
